screenconnect-cleanup.name: v1.8.13-beta.3 - Latest Beta - signature never blocks removal, Continue online
screenconnect-cleanup.body_html:
Latest beta. Replaces 1.8.13-beta.2 as the download used by the installer command.

Hosted Windows CI (Windows Server 2022 and 2025) passed. Confirmed on a real PC on November 25, 2026: the intruder's ScreenConnect that 1.8.13-beta.2 refused (signature status UnknownError) was removed.

Changes

  • Removal: the executable's digital signature no longer blocks removal. An intruder's ScreenConnect whose signature Windows does not confirm (status UnknownError, for example the revoked ConnectWise certificate) was refused with "PRODUCT VERIFICATION FAILED" and left installed. Unsigned, altered, re-signed and look-alike copies are now removed too. Unchanged: the instance must sit in a ScreenConnect directory, have a ScreenConnect binary name and (with a service) a ScreenConnect service name, and the technician still approves by typing. Anything other than a valid ConnectWise signature is written as a SIGNATURE WARNING to the log and the removal manifest. Files are quarantined, never deleted.
  • GUI: a finished Offline run shows Continue online next to Start over.
  • README: Defender false-positive note; what the ScreenConnect tray icon looks like, and to stage on a separate PC and run Offline first when it is there.

remote-diagnostics.name: Remote Diagnostics v2026-11-15.1
remote-diagnostics.body_html:
First public release.

Download remote-diagnostics-v2026-11-15.1.zip below, unzip it onto the PC and double-click Run-RemoteDiagGui.bat (it asks for administrator rights). Every tool also has its own Run-*.bat console launcher.

What's in it:

  • Pull logs from this PC or another one (WinRM): event logs, blue-screen and GPU/TDR decoding, minidumps, print queues and spooler errors, network state, startup items, EFI partition usage, one zip with a REVIEW LIST on top
  • Enable / revert remote diagnostics (turns itself off after 48 hours)
  • Deep persistence inventory, camera and startup check, wake-from-sleep device check
  • Print-freeze watcher and a WSD -> TCP/IP printer port fix
  • Boot-failure log collector for WinRE / WinPE

Windows 10 / 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1. See the README for the full guide.

student-times.name: Student Times v2026-11-23.1
student-times.body_html:
First public release.

Download student-times-v2026-11-23.1.zip below, unzip it onto the student PC and double-click Run-StudentTimes.bat (it asks for administrator rights).

What's in it:

  • Weekly logon-hours grid for one or many local accounts, applied with net user /times
  • Temporary unlock (today / 2 / 3 days) that re-locks by itself at midnight
  • Logout tasks kept in step with the grid, time-change rights removed, clock-sync check
  • Network Push: the same schedule to every PC in a classroom over WinRM
  • Desktop Lock: no wallpaper/theme changes, Windows Spotlight off, optional fixed lock-screen picture

Windows 10 / 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1. See the README for the full guide.

remote-access-tool-blocker.name: USE THIS - Stable v2026.10.14.3 (full kit + Windows-only)
remote-access-tool-blocker.body_html:
USE THIS - STABLE RELEASE

This is the stable release. Use these files:

  • full-kit-eset-2026.10.14.3.zip - programs 1 (Windows blocker) and 2 (ESET website list)
  • remote-tools-block-windows-2026.10.14.3.zip - Windows-only kit (no ESET)

An ALPHA build containing an unreleased experimental feature is published as a
separate prerelease. Do not use the alpha build - it is for testing only and
is not this stable release.

Verified on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7: both ZIPs here were built
from the exact commit below and downloaded back after upload with matching
per-member hashes.

2026.10.14.3 - Open list button

  • Add a third button, Open list, to program 2. It opens the existing import file in Notepad without rebuilding or changing the clipboard.
  • Keep BUILD and Open the list folder alongside it; disable all three while building.
  • If no list exists, show BUILD-first guidance without starting Notepad.
  • Windows regression tests exercise the real click handler, check the exact quoted path, unchanged file bytes, missing-file handling and busy state.

Earlier in 2026.10.14.x: BUILD copies the import file path (verified) and opens the list in Notepad; one combined ESET list instead of two; TeamViewer / AnyDesk / Splashtop / RustDesk unticked by default in both programs; coloured logging fixed.

Validation limits: Windows CI verifies control and launch behavior with intercepted process starts; visible Notepad and the manual ESET import remain owner live checks.

remote-access-tool-blocker.name: ALPHA - DO NOT USE - v2026.10.15.0-alpha.1 (Refresh list button)
remote-access-tool-blocker.body_html:
ALPHA - DO NOT USE

DO NOT USE THIS BUILD

This is an alpha prerelease containing an unfinished feature. It is published only
so the new feature can be looked at. Do not run it on a client PC.

Use the stable release instead: the release titled "USE THIS - Stable ..."
(currently v2026.10.14.3).

Both ZIPs here contain ALPHA-DO-NOT-USE.txt at the top level, and their program-1 window
title shows the alpha version, so an extracted copy cannot be mistaken for the stable kit.

What is new here (unproven)

Program 1 has a Refresh list button:

  • It asks for confirmation, then rebuilds the Windows App Control signer list from
    lolrmm.io in one step (Build-RmmAppControl -IncludeOptional).
  • It refuses cleanly on a PC that cannot build the policy (Windows Home, or no
    ConvertFrom-CIPolicy) and tells you to build it on a Pro PC.
  • It says plainly that an already-installed policy keeps the old list until BLOCK or
    Test mode is pressed again, so the new list is not silently assumed to be live.
  • It is disabled while work is running, like the other buttons.

Why it was added: the program list is baked into the shipped policy files and only changes
when a vendor changes its code-signing certificate. There was no way to refresh it from the
window, so an out-of-date kit had to be updated by hand from the repository.

What has been verified

  • Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 CI runs the real click handler with an
    injected confirmation answer and checks: declining does nothing, the build script is
    called once with -IncludeOptional, the success text tells the operator to press BLOCK,
    the buttons are re-enabled, and a PC that cannot build gets the clear message with no
    build attempt.
  • The ZIPs are built from the exact commit below and downloaded back after upload with
    matching per-member hashes.

What has NOT been verified

  • A real rebuild against live lolrmm.io from the button, and the on-screen confirmation
    dialog, have not been exercised on hardware.
  • Program 2 (ESET website list) and the Windows-only kit are unchanged from the stable
    release apart from the version string.
  • No owner live test has happened for this build.
